Open the map page
1
Aramco building hit in Riyadh (8 Nov)
Saudi Energy Ministry: falling shrapnel caused minor damage to an Aramco administrative building in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District; no injuries and no output loss confirmed.
2
Houthis claim Pumping Stn 8, Khurais (8 Nov)
The Houthis claimed strikes on East-West pipeline Pumping Station No. 8 at Dawadmi and on Aramco facilities at Khurais; not confirmed by Saudi Arabia (location approximate).
3
Tanker on fire 8 nm NW of Khasab (7 Nov)
UKMTO: a tanker caught fire about 8 nm north-west of Khasab at 19:20 UTC on 7 Nov and the crew were evacuated; another tanker was hit by a projectile outbound through the strait.
4
Only 11 Hormuz crossings (7 Nov), 6 dark
Windward counted 11 crossings on 7 Nov (3 tankers) against 84-140 a day pre-war; Kpler put October Hormuz crude at about 10.2 mb/d, 60% of pre-war (area approximate).
5
97 ships holding in Gulf (8 Nov), down from 197
straits.live counted 97 AIS-visible ships holding in the Strait and Gulf watch box on 8 Nov, against 147 on 7 Nov and 197 on 4 Nov; AIS coverage varies (area approximate).
6
Bypass routes >40% of Gulf exports
Kpler: pipelines avoiding Hormuz carry over 40% of regional exports vs 17% pre-war; Yanbu loadings 2.21 mb/d in 1-25 Oct vs 2.54 in September.
7
US disables M/V Huda (7 Nov)
CENTCOM says an aircraft disabled the St Kitts-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman after it tried to breach the blockade (position not given, approximate).
GULF OIL FLOWS · updated 9 Nov 2026

Less oil is leaving the Gulf than before the war: Kpler counts about 16.1 mb/d of crude and condensate across Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Oman in October (down about 1 mb/d from September), of which only about 10.2 mb/d of crude went through Hormuz itself, about 60% of the 17.1 mb/d pre-war level. Traffic through the strait remains very thin, with Windward counting 11 crossings on 7 Nov, over half of them dark, so the Yanbu and Fujairah bypass routes carry over 40% of exports while Iraq's Ceyhan route has risen to about 0.5 mb/d. Attacks continued over the weekend: a tanker burned about 8 nm north-west of Khasab on 7 Nov, the Houthis fired missiles at Riyadh on 8 Nov, damaging an Aramco building and claiming strikes on Khurais and an East-West pipeline pumping station (no output loss confirmed). Trump told CNN on 8 Nov that new strikes are 'highly unlikely' to be needed if Iran signs a strong agreement, while Araghchi says Iran's two-day Hormuz proposal stands but mediators have stopped travelling.

Alerts (6)

RED · Brent ▲ up · days · medium confidence
Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh damaged an Aramco building on 8 Nov, and the Houthis claim strikes on Khurais and East-West pipeline Pumping Station No. 8 at Dawadmi; Saudi Arabia confirms only minor shrapnel damage in Riyadh.
Yahya Saree / Saudi Energy Ministry, Houthi military spokesman / Saudi government
“The incident resulted in falling shrapnel that caused minor damage to the building, with no injuries or fatalities reported, thankfully”
Why it matters: Khurais and the East-West pumping stations feed the Yanbu bypass route that carries much of Saudi exports; a confirmed hit would remove export capacity while Hormuz remains constrained.

RED · Brent ▲ up · days · medium confidence
Update: A tanker caught fire about 8 nm north-west of Khasab on 7 Nov with its crew evacuated, another was hit by a projectile outbound through Hormuz, and the IRGC claims three more tankers burned on 8 Nov (unconfirmed).
UKMTO / IRGC, UK maritime agency / Iranian military
Why it matters: Continued attacks keep war-risk costs high and tanker traffic thin on the Omani side of the strait, slowing any recovery in Gulf exports.
Gulf News: UAE rescues 22 crew in Gulf of Oman as US tightens Iran blockade · Sat 07 Nov 19:20 UK · Open source
RED · Brent ▲ up · days · medium confidence
Trump confirmed 'minor' US strikes on an Iranian air-defence system on 6 Nov, CENTCOM disabled the St Kitts-flagged M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman on 7 Nov and set up Task Force Iron Gate, and the IRGC lifted its 2,000 km missile-range limit.
Donald Trump / CENTCOM / IRGC, US President / US military / Iranian military
Why it matters: Low-level US-Iran exchanges and a tighter blockade keep the risk of Iranian retaliation against Gulf shipping and export hubs alive, offsetting some of Trump's softer language.
ABC News (Australia): Explosions heard in Strait of Hormuz as Iran reviews de-escalation proposals · Sat 07 Nov 16:00 UK · Open source
AMBER · Brent ▼ down · days · medium confidence
Trump told CNN on 8 Nov that renewed strikes on Iran are 'highly unlikely' to be necessary if Tehran signs a strong agreement; Brent opened lower on Monday.
Donald Trump, US President
“The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary.”
Why it matters: It softens last week's 'you'll know soon enough' threat and cuts the near-term risk of a new US-Iran escalation, removing some war premium from Brent, though he added he would strike 'if necessary'.
Oilprice via Yahoo Finance: Oil Prices Fall as Trump Signals No New Attacks on Iran · Sun 08 Nov 19:39 UK · Open source
AMBER · Brent ▲ up · days · medium confidence
Update: Araghchi says Iran's two-day Hormuz proposal still stands but warned Washington to accept it or 'choose war', and said mediators have stopped travelling since the US midterm shock.
Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of Iran
“Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results.”
Why it matters: Iran keeps the door open to reopening Hormuz only on terms the US has not accepted, and the pause in Qatari and Pakistani shuttle diplomacy delays any relief for flows, which supports Brent.
Yahoo News: Iran Urges Washington To Accept 2-Day Proposal To End Hostilities Or Face Hell · Sun 08 Nov 18:22 UK · Open source
AMBER · Brent ▲ up · weeks · low confidence
Israeli Defence Minister Katz said the mission against Iran is 'still not complete', after Channel 12 reported a pre-election Netanyahu-Mossad operation against Iran was halted when the US learned of it (denied by Netanyahu's office).
Israel Katz, Defence Minister of Israel
“With regard to Iran, the mission is still not complete.”
Why it matters: Israeli strikes would likely draw Iranian retaliation against Gulf energy and shipping; the message contrasts with Trump's softer line and keeps an Israeli escalation risk in the price.
